content_units: U.S. IP Protection for a Coffee Business
For a small coffee business in the United States, these three protections cover different things:
-   Trademark   protects   brand identifiers   that tell customers who you are.
-   Copyright   protects   original creative expression   you made.
-   Patent   protects   new inventions or functional designs  .
Trademark vs Copyright vs Patent
Type   What it protects   What matters most   Typical coffee-business examples
Trademark   Names, logos, slogans, brand signals   Whether customers use it to identify your business as the source   Coffee shop logo, house blend name, shop name
Copyright   Original written, artistic, musical, and other expressive works   Whether the work is original and fixed in a tangible form   Original menu text, website copy, custom artwork

Patent   New, useful, and non-obvious inventions; some ornamental product designs   Whether the idea is novel and meets patent rules   Spill-resistant lid design, new closure mechanism, unique functional cup feature
What Each One Would Protect for Your Coffee Business
Trademark
A trademark would protect the   branding  , not the product idea itself.
-   Your logo   if you use it to identify your café or packaged coffee.
-   Your house blend name   if it functions as a brand name for that blend.
-   Your coffee shop name or slogan   if customers associate it with your business.
Important note: trademark does   not   protect the coffee recipe or the lid engineering.
Copyright
Copyright would protect the   creative expression   you wrote or designed.
-   Original menu text  , such as your descriptions of drinks and food.
-   Original website/about-page copy   describing your brand story.
-   Original artwork on the menu, packaging, or wall graphics   if created by you or properly assigned to your business.
Important note: copyright does   not   protect short names, titles, or most simple logos very well as brand rights; that is usually trademark territory.
Patent
A patent would protect the   invention or design   if it is new enough and meets legal requirements.
-   Your new spill-resistant lid design   if it has a new functional structure or mechanism.
-   A new venting or locking feature   in the lid that reduces spills.
-   A distinctive ornamental lid shape   may qualify for a   design patent   if the novelty is in appearance rather than function.
Important note: patents do   not   protect your blend name or menu wording.
Best Fit for the Items You Mentioned
-   Logo   → usually   Trademark  ; possibly also copyright if highly original artwork
-   House blend name   →   Trademark
-   Original menu text   →   Copyright
-   Spill-resistant lid design   →   Patent   if novel; possibly   design patent   for ornamental appearance
